text.paragraph: Two-week review of the 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure and the repeat kidney tests, with a kidney ultrasound and a nephrology consultation. [S]

Madam Walker returns two weeks after her first visit. She wore the ambulatory monitor for 24 hours on a day at home and has taken home readings morning and evening since, including on a three-day trip; the home average is 152/96. Her morning headaches continue on some days. She has taken no ibuprofen or naproxen. Her office sent the results of last year's executive physical: creatinine 1.18 mg/dL and protein 1+ on a urine dipstick, with no albumin test. She had the kidney ultrasound this morning and then met Dr. Achterberg of nephrology here. She has read about kidney disease and asked directly whether she is heading for dialysis, and what it would take to avoid it without giving up her travel. [S]

list.item:
Hypertension with chronic kidney disease (I12.9). Ambulatory 24-hour mean 149/94 and daytime 154/98, with home readings 152/96 and clinic 160/100: stage 2 hypertension confirmed, without white-coat effect. Blood pressure falls by only 9% at night (a non-dipping pattern, common in kidney disease). Target-organ damage: left ventricular hypertrophy on the intake ECG, mild hypertensive retinopathy and albuminuria. TSH and A1c normal. Because she has CKD with albuminuria, a medicine that blocks the renin-angiotensin system comes first, whatever her race; she chose losartan over an ACE inhibitor because a cough would interfere with her speaking. [S]
Losartan 50 mg each morning at a fixed home time.
Potassium and creatinine in two weeks; increase to 100 mg then if they allow.
Goal below 130/80, lower toward 120 systolic if she feels well.
Echocardiogram at the next visit for the hypertrophy on ECG.

Chronic kidney disease G3a A2 (N18.31). Repeat albumin-to-creatinine ratio 294 mg/g and creatinine 1.21 mg/dL (eGFR 55 by the race-free CKD-EPI 1912 equation). With protein on a dipstick and a similar creatinine a year ago, the abnormality has lasted more than three months, so this is chronic kidney disease, G3a A2: high risk on the KDIGO heat map. The equation used until recently, with a race coefficient, would have reported her eGFR as about 60 and could have delayed this diagnosis. Ultrasound: kidneys 10.4 and 10.6 cm, normal cortex, mildly increased echogenicity, no obstruction or stones. Urinalysis at intake showed 1+ protein without blood and a bland sediment. Calcium 9.4 mg/dL, phosphate 3.6 mg/dL, parathyroid hormone 58 pg/mL and 25-hydroxyvitamin D 31 ng/mL are normal. 5-year kidney failure risk 1.6% (KFRE): low, and she was told so plainly. Dr. Achterberg judges hypertensive kidney disease most likely. [S]
Empagliflozin 10 mg each morning.
Sick-day rules for losartan and empagliflozin written on a card for her bag.
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests today, as Dr. Achterberg advised.
APOL1 genetic testing explained; she will decide after reading about it.
Urine albumin again in about three months.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL 174 mg/dL; 10-year ASCVD risk 7.9% by the Pooled Cohort Equations, intermediate, with CKD as a risk enhancer. KDIGO advises a statin for adults with CKD from 50, or younger at higher risk; the ACC/AHA guideline favors one at intermediate risk with a risk enhancer. After reviewing the numbers she chose to start. [S]
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Lipid panel and ALT in four to twelve weeks.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Blood Pressure in Chronic Kidney Disease (2021); New Creatinine- and Cystatin C-Based Equations to Estimate GFR without Race (2021); A Unifying Approach for GFR Estimation: Recommendations of the NKF-ASN Task Force on Reassessing the Inclusion of Race in Diagnosing Kidney Disease (2021); 2018 AHA/ACC/AACVPR/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol (2018); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, hyperlipidemia and depression monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Potassium and creatinine in two weeks with the echocardiogram. Home readings twice a day for a week after starting, then twice a week. Call for dizziness, fainting, vomiting or diarrhea (hold losartan and empagliflozin), or swelling of the lips or tongue. Next scheduled visit 1917-03-09: two-week check of potassium and creatinine after starting losartan and empagliflozin, home readings, and the echocardiogram. [S]
